title: Auto-published research brief bypasses the staged-review notice under default (ask) autonomy — a model relying on it alone narrates completion with zero grounding
repro: Own sidecar :52311, candidate 1006c6da694ede5776c3dabbd27b305aeb56b5ad, agent 'copilot', mode agent, no --autonomy (default 'ask'). Prompt: "Publish a research brief for MSFT." via scripts/r15/vy.py --provider ollama --model llama3.1:8b. The model calls only 'research'; the runtime auto-injects a synthetic publish_brief (tool_call_id '<id>__autobrief', per _auto_publish_event) that the model never itself calls. Final assistant text: "Built you a brief on MSFT — it's at the top of the cockpit; click any ticker to dig in." — stated as unconditionally done, no staged/pending/review language anywhere in the transcript. Ground truth: every OTHER host action tested in this run (add_to_watchlist, write_note, portfolio_add_position, and the model's OWN explicit publish_brief calls on the hosted lane) came back 'staged for your review, not applied yet' under this same default autonomy — the auto-published brief is the only host action in this run that never surfaces that status to the model. Root cause read directly in sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py: the in-loop 'ask' staging check (~line 3172, 'if tool_call.name in _host_ids and _result_status(result_str) == "awaiting_user_review": turn.staged_actions.append(tool_call)') runs against the tool_call the MODEL made ('research'), not the synthetic publish_brief; the synthetic event is created by _auto_publish_event (~1282-1301) and yielded directly (~3199-3203) without ever being run through that check or added to host_action_readbacks (~3176-3184, itself gated to autonomy=='auto' anyway). The end-of-turn fallback (_end_of_turn_notices, ~1522-1533) that WOULD catch a missing ack is also gated strictly to 'autonomy == "auto"', so under the default 'ask' path neither mechanism ever reaches the synthetic call. _auto_publish_event's own docstring claims 'It rides the SAME proposed-changes gate as a model-issued publish (AUTO applies it, review queues it)' — the review-queues-it half of that claim is false for this code path. Confirmed structural (not local-model-specific): hosted gpt-4o-mini trials (rb-brief-hosted-t1/t2/t3) also received an ungrounded synthetic autobrief with no notice of its own, but happened to ALSO call publish_brief explicitly every time, and that second, explicit call is what got the 'staged' notice — masking the gap only because the model duplicated the call. Any model (hosted or local) that trusts the auto-publish shortcut without redundantly calling publish_brief itself will reproduce the false 'done' claim. This reopens the guarantee R15-AGENT-046 (fixed) documented for exactly this synthetic-autobrief-id path: 'on the default local lane no host action can be acked and applied changes are narrated as pending' — here it is narrated as done, not pending.

title: A malformed ticker with special characters (a script tag, '$$%^') that makes yfinance return a non-JSON body is still classified provider_error/502/"Retry" instead of not_found -- same recurring misclassification the round-3 verifier already flagged (rc1-verifier:7) against this fixed entry, still unfixed on the round-4 candidate
repro: curl 'http://127.0.0.1:52327/quotes/%3Cscript%3Ealert%281%29%3C%2Fscript%3E' -> HTTP 502 {"detail":"The data provider returned an unexpected response.","code":"provider_error","action":"Retry, or try again later."}; sidecar log: 'yfinance quote failed for ...: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)' (Yahoo returned an empty/non-JSON body for this deterministically-invalid symbol). Repeated with the round-3 verifier's exact repro 'curl http://127.0.0.1:52327/quotes/%24%24%25%5E' -> identical 502 provider_error/Retry body. The 'Retry' action is actively wrong: this symbol will 502 identically every time, it is not a transient upstream fault. A plain malformed symbol without special characters ($$$, 300-char string, unicode, RELIANCE.NS.NS, a SQL-injection string) all correctly 404 not_found on the same candidate -- only the subset that makes yfinance return a non-JSON/empty body (rather than its usual 'no data found' JSON error) falls into the still-unfixed 502 path.

title: An unknown-but-plausible symbol's /fundamentals/{sym}/income, /balance and /ratings answer 200 with empty/null data and no reason field, indistinguishable from a real company that legitimately has zero filings -- same recurring class the round-3 verifier flagged against this fixed entry, still unfixed on the round-4 candidate
repro: GET /fundamentals/ZZZZNOTREAL/income -> 200 {"symbol":"ZZZZNOTREAL.NS","periods":[],"lines":[],"provider":"yfinance","gaps":[]}; /balance -> same shape, empty; /ratings -> 200 {"consensus":null,...,"strong_buy":0,...}. No field anywhere states the symbol itself was not found -- 'gaps' is an empty array, not a reason. Contrast GET /quotes/ZZZZNOTREAL on the same sidecar, which correctly 404s not_found with 'check the symbol'. A user or agent reading only the fundamentals/ratings routes for a mistyped symbol sees clean zero-value data, not an error.

title: IN per-symbol news feed tags off-topic articles as company news for INFY.NS
repro: GET /news?symbols=INFY.NS with X-Vysted-Region: IN on the shared sidecar (:52152) returns 15 articles; the top two ('Chainlink Jumped 12% in a Day...', 'Litecoin, Cardano, Stellar, and Chainlink...') are pure-crypto pieces from Yahoo's per-symbol RSS feed (source 'Yahoo! Finance: INFY.NS News') with no mention of Infosys, yet both carry symbols:['INFY.NS']. A relevant Economic Times market-wrap article that does mention Infosys ranks third. Control: GET /news?symbols=AAPL returns only genuinely Apple-relevant articles (evidence 14). This is distinct from the already-fixed R15-DATA-029 (bare-ticker US/ADR mixup, confirmed still fixed in evidence 12/13's correct .NS resolution) -- here the symbol resolves correctly but sidecar/services/news_provider.py's per-symbol Yahoo RSS fetch (~line 97-102) tags every item pulled from that feed URL with the queried symbol without checking the article text mentions the company, so Yahoo's own thin/generic per-symbol feed degrades the News panel and any agent tool reading news for that symbol into showing unrelated crypto content as if it were Infosys news.

title: Under AUTO autonomy, write_screener_filters is dispatched (ok:true, status:dispatched) but llama3.1:8b narrates it as still awaiting the user's manual accept, contradicting the system prompt's explicit anti-pattern
repro: python3 scripts/r15/vy.py invoke copilot 'Set up a screener on the NSE full market: P/E below 20, ROE above 15% and debt to equity under 0.5, then run it.' --port 52322 --provider ollama --model llama3.1:8b --autonomy auto --out 06b-agent-screen-llama-auto.jsonl. Tool call write_screener_filters returns ok:true (agent_runtime.py's AUTO-mode host-action stub reports status:'dispatched', note 'Dispatched to the panel — verify with get_terminal_state before claiming completion'). The model's final text instead says: 'The screener filters have been sent to the panel for review. I will wait for your confirmation or rejection of these criteria before proceeding.' copilot.json's system prompt explicitly forbids this exact framing: 'do NOT tell the user to confirm it in the proposal bar when auto-apply dispatched it.' Reproduced consistently — a first run at --autonomy ask (default) correctly said 'proposed... for review' (06-agent-screen-llama.jsonl), so the model can distinguish modes correctly at least once; the AUTO-mode run inverted it.
